preconditions.description: The first line of input is an integer N (1 ≤ N ≤ 10) representing the number of categories.
Each of the next N lines contains a category name, an integer W (1 ≤ W ≤ 10), and W unique words associated with the category.

preconditions.expression: all(len(word) <= 30 and word.islower() and word.isalpha() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:N+1] for word in line.split()[2:])
preconditions.description: All words in category descriptions are lowercase alphabetic strings of length at most 30.

preconditions.expression: all(len(word) <= 30 and word.islower() and word.isalpha() for line in stdin.splitlines()[N+1:] for word in line.split())
preconditions.description: All words in the problem statement are lowercase alphabetic strings of length at most 30.
The problem statement consists of between 1 and 10000 lines of words.

postconditions.expression: all(line.strip() in [category for category, _, _ in categories] for line in stdout.splitlines())
postconditions.description: Each line of output is a category name that was suggested as having the highest number of matches.

postconditions.expression:
max_matches := max(category_matches.values(), default=0)
all(category_matches[category] == max_matches for category in stdout.splitlines())
postconditions.description: The output contains only categories whose total word matches equal the maximum number of matches among all categories.

postconditions.expression: stdout.splitlines() == sorted(set(category for category in stdout.splitlines()))
postconditions.description: The output contains each suggested category exactly once, sorted lexicographically.

candidate_issues.instruction: Add a postcondition to ensure that the total word matches for each category are computed correctly by counting exact word matches (not substrings) in the problem statement.
candidate_issues.task_evidence: Note that words that are part of other words do not count. For example, the word statement should not count as an occurrence for the word ate.

candidate_issues.instruction: Add a postcondition to ensure that the total word matches for a category are the sum of occurrences of all its associated words in the problem statement.
candidate_issues.task_evidence: If there were 3 occurrences each of the words vertex and edge, the number of matches for the category graph would be 6.

candidate_issues.instruction: Add a postcondition to ensure that the `category_matches` dictionary is constructed by counting exact word matches for each category's associated words across the entire problem statement.
candidate_issues.task_evidence: If the statement contained 14 occurrences of words and 4 of letters, the number of matches for the category string would be 18.

candidate_issues.instruction: Add a postcondition to ensure that the problem statement is processed as a whole (all lines concatenated into a single list of words) before counting word matches.

candidate_issues.instruction: Add a postcondition to ensure that the output categories are determined by the maximum total word matches across all categories.
